inputs.modified_text:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court under Justice Sumeet Goel has handed down another decision that weakens the very tools needed to uphold order. They've ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be canceled simply because stolen articles were not recovered or the allegations are serious. Revocation only follows clear proof of misuse of liberty or other supervening circumstances, and in this instance they dismissed the plea to revoke the pre-arrest bail outright.

This is yet another clear advantage handed to the accused at the direct expense of victims and real accountability. It places legal technicalities above personal responsibility and reveals how these courts routinely disregard the authority required to safeguard families, homes, and the social order that has preserved communities across generations. When institutions hesitate to impose genuine consequences, ordinary families absorb the harm, and we witness the steady erosion of the discipline and cultural continuity that once kept society intact.
